name: GitHub Copilot
tagline: AI coding assistant integrated with GitHub and editors

pricing.notes: Official GitHub Copilot plan docs checked 2026-07-30; Pro listed at $10/month, with usage-credit changes in 2026.

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: 2,000 code completions/month; AI-credit allowance exists but its numeric amount is not publicly stated; automatic model selection only.

tiers.name: Student
tiers.limits: Unlimited code completions; AI-credit allowance exists but its numeric amount is not publicly stated.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: 1,500 AI credits/month: 1,000 base plus 500 Flex; unlimited code completions.
tiers.notes: For new subscriptions under the June 2026 billing model.

tiers.name: Pro+
tiers.limits: 7,000 AI credits/month: 3,900 base plus 3,100 Flex; unlimited code completions.
tiers.notes: For new subscriptions under the June 2026 billing model.

tiers.name: Max
tiers.limits: 20,000 AI credits/month: 10,000 base plus 10,000 Flex; unlimited code completions.

tiers.name: Business
tiers.limits: Standard allowance is 1,900 AI credits/user/month; temporary June-August 2026 promotion raises it to 3,000 through August 31, 2026.

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Standard allowance is 3,900 AI credits/user/month; temporary June-August 2026 promotion raises it to 7,000 through August 31, 2026.

pricing.freeTierCaps: 2,000 code completions/month; AI-credit quantity is not publicly stated; automatic model selection only
pricing.billingTerms: new individual subscriptions are monthly only; legacy annual Pro/Pro+ subscriptions remain on the old request model until renewal
pricing.hiddenCosts: Extra AI credits cost $0.01 each and unused monthly credits do not roll over; Copilot code review can also consume separately billed GitHub Actions minutes.

verdictSummary: You can use open-source editor agents and local/API models, but Copilot's value is editor integration, model routing, GitHub context, completions, and managed usage.
coreLoopDIY: Install an open-source IDE assistant, connect model APIs or a local model, index the repo, and generate code/edit suggestions.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because low-latency completion and repo-aware coding are available in their editor without setup.

priorArt.name: Continue
priorArt.desc: Open-source coding assistant extension that connects to local or hosted models.

alternatives.name: Cline
alternatives.desc: A code agent in your editor; the model bill is still yours.

facts.install: Install from the VS Code or JetBrains marketplace, or install the Cline CLI
facts.engines: Cline account models or bring-your-own-key providers including Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, Azure, Bedrock, Vertex and OpenRouter, plus local Ollama and LM Studio models
facts.dataFormat: Repository edits stay in the local workspace; extension/session settings are local, while selected workspace context and prompts go to the chosen model provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It is agent-first and separately model-billed, with weaker low-latency inline completions and GitHub-native integration than Copilot.
facts.setupBlocker: Sign in to Cline or configure a provider API key or local model

alternatives.name: Kilo Code
alternatives.desc: One open agent across VS Code, JetBrains and the terminal; inference still has a meter somewhere.

alternatives.name: OpenCode
alternatives.desc: A fast local coding agent with no loyalty to any model vendor.

facts.install: Install with the shell script, Homebrew, npm or Bun; a desktop app is also available
facts.engines: A broad provider catalog covering hosted, OpenAI-compatible and local model endpoints, including optional OpenCode Zen or Go services
facts.dataFormat: Project files remain local; configuration, sessions and snapshot metadata are local, and a session is uploaded only when the user explicitly shares it, while prompts go to the chosen provider
facts.gapVsPaid: It is agent-first and lacks Copilot's equally seamless inline completions and integration across GitHub and existing editors.
facts.setupBlocker: Configure a provider credential or local model unless using a separately billed OpenCode model service

alternatives.name: Tabby
alternatives.desc: Copilot-shaped completions and chat, paid for with your own GPU instead of a seat.

facts.install: Run the server from Docker or a standalone binary, then connect an editor extension
facts.engines: Local llama.cpp-backed completion, chat and embedding models or separately configured remote HTTP model endpoints
facts.dataFormat: Models, configuration, logs, indexed source and Tabby's database live under TABBY_ROOT, which defaults to the user's .tabby directory
facts.gapVsPaid: Completion quality and latency depend on the chosen model and hardware, and the GitHub and editor experience is less turnkey than Copilot.
facts.setupBlocker: Download and size suitable models, provide enough GPU or RAM, start the server, and configure each editor client

alternatives.name: Zed
alternatives.desc: A fast open editor with completions, chat and agents built in; model usage is separate.

facts.install: Install the native app from Zed or an operating-system package manager on macOS, Linux or Windows
facts.engines: Zed-hosted models, bring-your-own-key providers, local Ollama, LM Studio or llama.cpp models, and ACP-compatible coding agents
facts.dataFormat: Project files stay on the local or SSH-accessed machine and app state is local; hosted or BYOK prompts go to the selected provider, while collaboration state uses Zed's cloud
facts.gapVsPaid: It requires switching editors, while model usage is separate and Copilot works across more existing editors and GitHub surfaces.
facts.setupBlocker: None for the editor itself; AI requires a Zed account, provider key, local model, or external agent

rejectedAlternatives.name: Continue
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Acquired by Cursor; the repo is read-only and 2.0.0 is the last release.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Refact
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The original repo was archived and Refact Cloud was retired in May 2026.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Roo Code
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The extension shut down and the repo was archived on May 15, 2026.

notes: Very relevant to the site's own audience; verdict is nuanced because the app is partly wrapper, partly platform.
prompt:
Build me a local-first coding assistant setup to replace GitHub Copilot. Requirements:

- Do not build or train a model. Set up the open-source Continue extension in
  VS Code, configured against models I control.
- Chat and edit model: Claude or GPT over API, key referenced from my
  environment, never committed. Autocomplete model: a small local coder model
  served by Ollama, so completions are free and work offline.
- Deliver the actual Continue config file with both models wired, plus
  sensible keybindings for inline edit and chat.
- Enable Continue's codebase indexing for repo-aware answers; document where
  the index lives and how to rebuild it.
- Add scripts/ai-review.sh: pipes `git diff` to the API model (key from .env)
  and prints a short pre-commit review.
- Everything local except the chat-model API calls; turn off the extension's
  telemetry in the config.
- Out of scope: writing an editor extension from scratch, GitHub PR-bot
  features, team seat management.
- README: Ollama install and model pull commands, where keys go, and an honest
  note that local autocomplete is slower and dumber than Copilot's, that is
  the trade for free and private.
